title: Gabber modification preserving relative logarithmic smoothness
statement:
A trait is $\operatorname{Spec}R$ for a Noetherian local domain of dimension one with principal maximal ideal. It is complete strictly henselian if $R$ is complete for that ideal, is henselian (simple roots of monic polynomials over its residue field lift), and has separably closed residue field. Its canonical log structure is $\mathcal O\cap j_*\mathcal O_\eta^\times$, where $j$ includes its generic point. Mixed characteristic means fraction-field characteristic zero and positive residue characteristic.

Let $T$ be a complete strictly henselian trait with its canonical fs log structure. Let $(V,M_V)$ be an integral log regular fs log scheme, quasi-projective of finite type over $T$, and log smooth over $T$ [def-trf-fs-log-blowup], [def-per-fs-log-smooth-etale], [def-pc-integral-scheme], [def-weil-finite-type-morphism]. Quasi-projective over a scheme $B$ means admitting a locally closed immersion into some $\mathbf P^n_B$; projective means a closed immersion into some $\mathbf P^n_B$ followed by projection [def-kun-projective]. Let a finite group $H$ act on $(V,M_V)$ over $T$. Suppose the action is tame: at every geometric point $\bar v$, its stabilizer has order prime to the residue characteristic (no restriction in characteristic zero). Suppose it is generically free: $H$ acts freely on a dense invariant open of $V$. There are an integral fs log scheme $(W,M_W)$ quasi-projective of finite type over $T$ and an $H$-equivariant projective birational log morphism $h:W\to V$, such that $W$ is log regular and log smooth over $T$, and the scheme quotient $Q=W/H$ has an fs log structure for which it is log regular and log smooth over $T$. Here birational modification means that $h$ restricts to an isomorphism between dense opens. The quotient is the categorical geometric quotient, affine locally given by invariant rings; its log structure is the invariant direct image of $M_W$. The boundary of $W$ is allowed to contain the inverse image of the nonfree locus, even when that locus meets the generic fibre.

source.place: Expose X Theorem 1.1, pp.135--136; Expose VI Theorem 3.2, pp.73--74; application in XVI 3.7, p.254. Complete traits and their finite-type schemes meet the noetherian quasi-excellent hypotheses.

proof.text: Write $T=\operatorname{Spec}R$. By [lem-per-complete-local-excellence], $R$ is excellent, so $T$ is quasi-excellent. The finite-type map $V\to T$ and [lem-per-quasi-excellent-finite-type-stability] make $V$ quasi-excellent and Noetherian (finite type includes quasi-compactness). The trait with its canonical chart $\mathbf N\to R$, $1\mapsto\pi$, is log regular directly: at its closed point the log ideal is $(\pi)$, the quotient is the residue field of dimension zero and the characteristic rank is one; at the generic point the characteristic is zero and the local ring is a field. Quasi-projectivity makes $V$ separated over the affine separated trait, hence separated absolutely. Here projective space is separated by [lem-trf-projective-bundle-separated]; the locally closed immersion defining quasi-projectivity is separated, since its diagonal is an isomorphism onto the appropriate fibre product. By [lem-trf-log-regular-divisorial-structure], the log structure of $V$ is the divisorial structure of its dense triviality open. Its map to $T$ is a map of the resulting log regular pairs. Indeed the pullback of the uniformizer is a log section; at a point of the triviality locus it is a unit, so that point maps to the generic point of $T$.

Apply the absolute four-stage construction [lem-per-gabber-absolute-equivariant-modification] to $(V,M_V,H)$. Its hypotheses are Step 1 and the assumed tame generically free action. Denote its final source by $W$ and its composite by $h$. Already $W$ is integral, fs log regular and quasi-projective of finite type over $T$; $h$ is equivariant, projective in the required finite-projective-space convention and an isomorphism over a dense invariant open. Its boundary is the inverse image of the original boundary together with the nonfree locus. The action on $W$ is very tame. We must check relative log smoothness along this particular construction, since it does not follow from its absolute conclusion.

source.place: VIII 1.1 and 5.6.1; X proof of 1.1, opening paragraph, p.139.

proof.text: The first two stages are saturated log blowup towers. They are log etale by [lem-per-log-smooth-composition-strict-base-change]. Their composites with the initial log-smooth map to $T$ are therefore log smooth. The induction starts with the given log smoothness of $V/T$. At the end of these two stages the scheme is regular and the boundary is $H$-strict strict normal crossings, exactly as required by the fixed-locus chart lemma used next.

At a nontrivial fixed-locus blowup in the third stage, apply [lem-per-gabber-fixed-locus-log-chart]. Work in its local model $Y/\Sigma$, with $\gamma:Q\to\mathbf Z^t\oplus\mathbf N^r$. On a $z_i$ chart the group map $1\oplus\beta_i$ is an automorphism of the group completion: its inverse sends $e_j$ to $e_j-e_i$ for $j\le m$, $j\ne i$, and fixes the remaining basis vectors. Thus the composed base map is injective and has the same cokernel as $\gamma^{\rm gp}$. On a $y_i$ chart, $1\oplus\delta$ is injective with free cokernel $\mathbf Z$; projection of a lattice vector $(a_1,\ldots,a_r,b)$ to $b-\sum_{j\le m}a_j$ identifies that cokernel with $\mathbf Z$. Therefore the cokernels of the two base maps fit into $0\to\operatorname{coker}\gamma^{\rm gp}\to\operatorname{coker}((1\oplus\delta)\gamma)^{\rm gp}\to\mathbf Z\to0$. This sequence splits by choosing a preimage of $1$, so its torsion is exactly the invertible torsion of $\operatorname{coker}\gamma^{\rm gp}$. In both kinds of charts the remaining variables are polynomial variables, so the comparison is smooth. The criterion [def-per-fs-log-smooth-etale] proves log smoothness on every chart. The blowup/strict-transform comparison and strict base-change locality in [lem-per-log-smooth-composition-strict-base-change] carry this calculation back to the original scheme. Apply this argument successively to the finite third-stage procedure. At every stage the induction hypothesis is log smoothness over $T$, and permissibility preserves the regular strict boundary supplied by the absolute construction.

At the fourth stage use [lem-per-gabber-abelian-stage-toric-chart]. Its input hypotheses now hold: the preceding stage is regular with strict $H$-strict boundary, free off it, with abelian inertia, and is log smooth over $T$. Put $\overline P=P\oplus\mathbf N^s$. The group map $Q^{\rm gp}\to\overline P^{\rm gp}$ is injective and its cokernel has the original invertible torsion, since the added factor is free. The image lies in $\overline R^{\rm gp}$. Consequently $\overline R^{\rm gp}/Q^{\rm gp}$ is a subgroup of $\overline P^{\rm gp}/Q^{\rm gp}$, and its torsion has invertible order. Transport through $\overline R^{\rm gp}\simeq\overline R'^{\rm gp}$. The retained boundary has group $R'^{\rm gp}\subset\overline R'^{\rm gp}$, contains the image of $Q^{\rm gp}$, and therefore $R'^{\rm gp}/Q^{\rm gp}$ is again a subgroup of that same cokernel. Its torsion is finite of invertible order. Thus $Q\to R'$ meets the log smooth chart criterion. Moreover the scheme map from the quotient chart is smooth: $\Lambda[\overline R']=\Lambda[R'][x_{c+1},\ldots,x_b]$. This proves log smoothness of the fourth-stage quotient chart over $\operatorname{Spec}\Lambda[Q]$, and hence over $T$ after the strict base change. The local identifications and comparisons in the toric chart lemma make these charts cover the quotient. Locality [lem-per-log-smooth-composition-strict-base-change] gives log smoothness of that quotient over $T$.

source.place: X 1.8, pp.146--148, especially (1.c)--(1.d) and the final paragraph.

proof.text: The absolute construction makes $W$ quasi-projective over the affine Noetherian trait. By [lem-per-projective-finite-group-quotient], its categorical geometric scheme quotient $q:W\to Q$ exists, is finite surjective, is affine locally computed by invariant rings, and is quasi-projective of finite type over $T$. The finite-quotient assertion gives an invariant affine cover by taking inverse images of affine opens of $Q$, so the action on $W$ is admissible. It is generically free because $h$ is an equivariant isomorphism over a dense free open. Apply [lem-per-very-tame-log-quotient]: the log structure is precisely $(q_*M_W)^H$, it is fs log regular, and $q$ is Kummer etale, in particular log etale. Its local quotient structures agree with Step 5 by the quotient and toric identifications. Thus $Q\to T$ is log smooth, and composition [lem-per-log-smooth-composition-strict-base-change] gives log smoothness of $W\xrightarrow qQ\to T$. The factorization of the invariant log map $W\to T$ through $Q$ is part of the quotient lemma. Together with Step 2 these are all conclusions. The enlarged boundary includes the nonfree locus without a special-fibre restriction, exactly as the source construction requires.

proof_origin.place: VIII four-stage absolute modification; X proof of Theorem 1.1, 1.3--1.8, pp.139--148; VI Theorem 3.2.

reviewed.note: mechanical checks by tools/merge_delivery.py; mathematics reviewed in full by NT-cc-Q18-66c96b64c (reviewer sub-agent of L); spot-checked: Read the item, all five new nodes and every cited statement in full, against ILO VIII 1.1–1.2, 4.1.5–4.2.13; X 1.1–1.10 (preparation 1.2, 1.3(vii), Lemmas 1.5–1.6, the Ui/Vi charts of 1.7, the 1.8 invariant monoids R̄ = Ker χ ∩ P̄ and R ⊂ R′ ⊂ R̄′); VI 3.1–3.5; and the XVI 3.7 application. The statement is unchanged apart from expanding the combined brackets, and it matches X 1.1 over a complete strictly henselian trait. Step 1: complete local gives excellent; finite type gives qe and Noetherian; separatedness checked; the trait's log-regularity dimension check holds; the map is one of log regular pairs. Step 2 takes only the absolute conclusions (VIII 1.2 shows h is not log smooth). Step 3: the first two stages are saturated log blowups, hence log étale. Step 4: I checked β_i^{-1}, the Vi cokernel map b−Σa_j and the split sequence. snc is kept because the blowups are permissible, and G-strictness by VIII 4.1.5. A (Z/2)² test on A² shows the strict-transform centres are locally fixed loci of subgroups of the inertia. Step 5: the subgroup-torsion argument for R̄^gp and R′^gp and the affine-space clause hold, and the quotient commutes with base change because |G| is invertible in Λ. Step 6: the quotient is admissible and generically free, the very-tame quotient is Kummer étale, and composition gives W→T log smooth. New nodes: all true, statement-only, not restatements, with small cases tested; none cites SGA. Two are strict generalizations of Q70's lem-per-gabber-equivariant-log-modification and lem-per-very-tame-quotient-log-regular (maintainer may repoint later). There is no existing general log-smooth chart-calculus node. Tool uses accepted: lem-trf-projective-bundle-separated and lem-trf-log-regular-divisorial-structure. Batch-5: the closures of every flagged citation contain only generic trf definitions or algebra (fs log/log-regular-pair definitions, universally catenary/CM, G-ring/J-2 locality, Proj separated, Kato–Nizioł toric local algebra). There is no thm-trf, trace transport, Poincaré duality or batch-4 node, so all flags are accepted. Advisory: the inherited stmt_dep def-weil-regular-scheme is unused but harmless. No fixes.

lean.statement: theorem exists_gabber_logSmooth_equivariant_modification (R : CommRingCat.{u}) [IsDomain R] [IsDiscreteValuationRing R] [IsAdicComplete (IsLocalRing.maximalIdeal R) R] [IsStrictlyHenselianLocalRing R] (T : FineSaturatedLogScheme.{u}) (e : T.scheme ≅ Spec R) (hcanonical : ∃ c : T.logStructure.monoidSheaf.obj ≅ divisorialLogPresheaf (Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom (algebraMap R (FractionRing R))) ≫ e.inv), c.hom ≫ divisorialStructuralMap (Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom (algebraMap R (FractionRing R))) ≫ e.inv) = T.logStructure.alpha) (V : FineSaturatedLogScheme.{u}) [IsIntegral V.scheme] (f : EtaleLogHom V T) (hregular : V.IsLogRegular) (hsmooth : f.IsLogSmooth) [LocallyOfFiniteType f.base] [QuasiCompact f.base] (hqp : ∃ (N : ℕ) (i : V.scheme ⟶ ℙ(ULift.{u} (Fin (N + 1)); T.scheme)), IsImmersion i ∧ i ≫ ℙ(ULift.{u} (Fin (N + 1)); T.scheme) ↘ T.scheme = f.base) (H : Type v) [Group H] [Finite H] (a : FSLogGroupAction H V) (hover : ∀ g : H, (a.logMap g).CompEq f f) (htame : a.IsTame) (hfree : a.IsGenericallyFree) : ∃ (W : FineSaturatedLogScheme.{u}) (b : FSLogGroupAction H W) (h : EtaleLogHom W V) (s : EtaleLogHom W T) (Q : FineSaturatedLogScheme.{u}) (q : EtaleLogHom W Q) (t : EtaleLogHom Q T), IsIntegral W.scheme ∧ LocallyOfFiniteType s.base ∧ QuasiCompact s.base ∧ (∃ (N : ℕ) (i : W.scheme ⟶ ℙ(ULift.{u} (Fin (N + 1)); T.scheme)), IsImmersion i ∧ i ≫ ℙ(ULift.{u} (Fin (N + 1)); T.scheme) ↘ T.scheme = s.base) ∧ h.CompEq f s ∧ b.IsEquivariant a h ∧ IsHProjective h.base ∧ (∃ d : W.scheme.PartialIso V.scheme, d.source.ι ≫ h.base = d.iso.hom ≫ d.target.ι) ∧ W.IsLogRegular ∧ s.IsLogSmooth ∧ b.IsQuotient q ∧ q.CompEq t s ∧ Q.IsLogRegular ∧ t.IsLogSmooth
